title: TwinFlow: safe request replay pipeline and cost budgeting
creator: Aisha Kaur
description:
Goal:
Build a production-safe request replay (TwinFlow) pipeline that lets PMs/ML engineers run non-intrusive replays of live requests against candidate model variants for canaries and A/B experiments while enforcing strict cost and tenant isolation guarantees. TwinFlow must support dynamic sampling policies, per-tenant budget fences, end-to-end tracing of replayed requests, and automatic rollback triggers based on quality/regression signals.

Problem and motivation:
Existing ad-hoc replays are either too expensive (full duplication) or risk cross-tenant contamination when replayed requests create state (cached keys, mutable third-party calls). We need a formalized pipeline that reduces observable risk while producing representative evaluation traffic for model lifecycle decisions (canary pass/fail, A/B metrics, quality regressions).

Acceptance criteria:
- Replay stream can be enabled per-route with a config that specifies sample rate, tenant whitelist, and cost cap.
- Replayed requests are tagged and isolated: separate quota buckets, no write-side effects in customer-facing stores, and KV cache partitioning to avoid collisions.
- Adaptive sampling engine that reduces sampling when budget burn rate exceeds threshold; policy is pluggable and uses exponential backoff + reservoir sampling to preserve rare-event coverage.
- Observable metrics: request coverage, replay latency distribution, token cost per minute, regression score (BLEU/ROUGE/LLM-eval) and auto-rollback signal if regression delta > threshold for X minutes.
- Rollback behavior: automatic traffic stop and notify on-call with runbook link; safe fallback to pinned stable model variant.

Non-goals:
- This ticket does not implement routed live canary traffic (real-serving split) or long-term persisted replay storage for privacy audits — those are separate follow-ups.

Design notes / constraints:
- Do not hold live request bodies for more than 24h; use ephemeral IDs and short-lived encryption keys.
- All replayed calls should run in the dedicated replay pool to avoid impacting live capacity. Replay pool uses scaled-down GPUs with lower priority.
- Trace propagation: replayed requests must include original trace_id and a twinflow_id to link live vs replayed responses in observability.
- Cost control: implement per-tenant minute-level token budget and a global soft cap with graceful throttling of sampling.
- Safety: add a "dry-run" mode that executes model inference but drops outputs before any post-processing step that could have downstream side effects.
comments: 2025-02-12 - Kickoff: scoped initial MVP with Product + Security. Decided to prioritize per-tenant budget fences over global-only caps (PM request after customer incident).

2025-02-18 - Prototype: implemented replay tagging and a replay worker pool that runs in a separate autoscaling group. Initial bench: replay worker throughput ~120 rps on a g4dn.xlarge equiv node accounting for 512-token median length.
2025-02-22 - Security review notes (from Maya Patel): ensure replay data encryption in transit and at rest; redact PII via existing sanitizer before enqueue. Added sanitizer hook to pipeline.

2025-02-25 - Design review: agreed on adaptive sampling algorithm (reservoir + exponential decay). Trade-off: simple deterministic sampling makes debugging easier but misses burst coverage; we selected hybrid reservoir seeded by deterministic hash for reproducibility.

2025-03-01 - Infra check: confirmed replay pool isolation prevents KV cache collisions by prefixing all cache keys with twinflow:<twinflow_id>. Will add automated tests to verify no shared keys with live pool.
2025-03-03 - QA plan: synthetic replay test that asserts no writes to production stores and validates rollback trigger by injecting regression marker into eval pipeline. QA owner: Sofia Martin.
2025-03-05 - Action items before canary: 1) Add per-tenant budget shaper with alerting, 2) Wire up auto-rollback signal to rollout controller, 3) Create runbook for on-call.
